Children and youth suicide help-seeking: most cases involve family issues

According to provisional statistics from the Coroner's Court, Hong Kong recorded 1,019 suicide deaths in 2025, a decrease of 10% from the previous year. The overall suicide rate fell from 15.1 per 100,000 population in 2024 to 13.57, reaching a new low since 2020. However, deaths in the children and adolescents category rose from 35 last year by more than 30% to 47, with the suicide rate in this group climbing from 3.4 per 100,000 in 2024 to 4.72 — a near 40% increase and the highest in nearly a decade. Organisations point to a polarised trend of overall stabilisation coupled with localised deterioration.

Centre director Wai Shiu-kei stressed that a person's suicide is never caused by a single factor, and that family problems — "most likely parent-child relationships, and possibly involving some academic factors, leading to escalating family conflicts" — are the most common.

Suicide Crisis Intervention Centre's Wai Shiu-kei said many suicide help-seeking cases involve family issues, which may also be driven by academic factors that escalate into family conflicts.

Call to expand three-tier emergency mechanism to include suicide prevention organisations

In response to the worsening problem of student suicides, the government launched the "three-tier emergency mechanism" in 2023 and made it a regular programme in secondary schools in 2025. Why, after nearly three years of implementation, have student suicide cases risen rather than fallen?

Wai Shiu-kei explained that under the current mechanism, the first tier is handled within schools based on students' situations, the second tier provides external support from community non-profit organisations, and the third tier involves principals referring high-risk students to psychiatric outpatient clinics. She considers the shortfall to lie in the second tier of community support outside school, where there is currently a lack of any organisations providing suicide prevention services. "If the student is not mentally ill, they may be discharged quickly, but there is no follow-up afterwards," she said.

She reiterated that suicide does not solely involve mental health issues and that a dual-track referral system should be considered, referring students simultaneously to psychiatric services and dedicated suicide prevention organisations for follow-up — "which I believe would yield better results." Chief executive Cheng Chung said that preventing youth suicide requires services spanning from early childhood through adolescence, but the current mechanism does not include suicide prevention organisations capable of long-term case follow-up. He urged the government to expand the mechanism to incorporate suicide prevention organisations as collaborating partners and to improve the data collection system for student suicides.

Chief executive Cheng Chung recommended expanding the three-tier emergency mechanism to incorporate suicide prevention organisations as supporting units.

Elderly suicides decline for fourth consecutive year yet still top the chart; overall suicide rate remains above international level

Last year, a total of 257 suicide deaths were recorded among those aged 70 or above, with a suicide rate of 21.1 per 100,000 population — the lowest in nearly a decade and a fourth consecutive year of decline. Nevertheless, this group still recorded the highest number of deaths among all age categories. Cheng Chung noted that the centre handles many help-seeking cases involving elderly individuals, and that the pandemic and emigration wave have left many seniors living alone and facing loneliness.

The centre pointed out that although Hong Kong's overall suicide rate has fallen to a new low since 2020, it remains above international levels, reflecting that suicide prevention work continues to face严峻 challenges.
